prompt: AVEVA's Python sample writes one value with POST to /streams/{WebId}/value. Which HTTP status does it expect on success?
explanation: Both the single-value write and the 100-value write to /recorded return 202 (Accepted) in AVEVA's sample. A PUT to a static attribute value returns 204. Testing for 200 is a listed mistake.

options.text: A list of AFValue objects only

explanation: PIconnect documents the result as "essentially a decorated version of a pandas.Series", which makes it easy to analyse in Python.

prompt: Which PowerShell Tools for the PI System cmdlet starts a Data Archive backup in OSIsoft's samples?
explanation: OSIsoft samples use Start-PIBackup -BackupLocation <dir> -Connection $con and poll Get-PIBackupState. "Backup-PIDataArchive" does not appear in any source seen.

prompt: What is the module name of PowerShell Tools for the PI System, as used in Get-Command -Module <name>?
explanation: The module is OSIsoft.PowerShell, installed under %pihome%\OSIsoft.PowerShell and auto-imported on first use.

prompt: Which practices do the sources warn against in production scripts? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Secure(0) in a JMP JSL script
Hard-coding a password in the script

explanation: Disabling certificate verification (verify=False in Python, Secure(0) in JSL) and hard-coding credentials are listed pitfalls; Kerberos avoids storing passwords. Sending X-Requested-With on writes is required, not a risk.

prompt: Connecting an integration platform that cannot do Kerberos.
scenario:
An integration platform must read PI data through PI Web API. Its HTTP client supports Basic and Bearer but not Kerberos. PI Web API is installed with default authentication.

What change does the Cybus integration guide describe?

options.text: Add Basic to the PI Web API AuthenticationMethods configuration item
Disable HTTPS so no authentication is needed
Remove Kerberos and enable both Bearer and Kerberos

explanation: Cybus Connectware does not support Kerberos, so Basic must be added to the PI Web API AuthenticationMethods configuration item; Kerberos is enabled by default. Disabling HTTPS is not possible, and Anonymous is advised against.

prompt: PIconnect is asked for PI.PIServer('NoSuchServer'). What happens?

options.text: A warning is raised and the default server is returned
PIconnect creates a new server entry
The call blocks until the server appears

explanation: If a named server is not found, "a warning is raised" and the default server is returned. That makes typos easy to miss, so check which server you got.

prompt: Match each PowerShell Tools cmdlet to its purpose.
explanation: Connect-PIDataArchive opens a connection; Get-PIPoint reads point configuration; Get-PIValue reads values; Add-PIValue writes values; Get-PIArchiveFileInfo lists archive files; Start-PIBackup starts a backup.

prompt: In which time zone do PowerShell Tools for the PI System display timestamps?

options.text: The PI Data Archive's local time
The time zone of the AF database

explanation: The 2015 PI Square blog notes that PowerShell Tools show timestamps in UTC, which surprises users who expect local time.

prompt: Which Python string is the safe way to pass the AF path Plant1\Outlet to PIconnect's database.descendant()?
explanation: Write AF paths as raw strings (r"Plant1\Outlet") or escape the backslashes; otherwise sequences such as \O may be treated as escapes.

prompt: In PIconnect's recorded_values, what does %tag% mean in filter_expression="'%tag%' > 100 and '%tag%' < 115"?

options.text: It is replaced with the tag name of the point
It is a wildcard matching any tag
It means the percentage of good values
It refers to the previous value

explanation: PIconnect replaces %tag% with the point's tag name, so the filter applies to the point's own values.

prompt: Put the steps of AVEVA's Python read-then-write pattern in order.

items.text: Read WebId from the response JSON

explanation: Create the auth object, GET the attribute by path, take its WebId from the JSON, GET recorded values with that WebId, then POST a value with the X-Requested-With header.

prompt: Why does AVEVA's transfer-verification PowerShell sample read values with -Count instead of an end time?

options.text: To avoid differences caused by snapshot data
Because -EndTime is not supported by Get-PIValue
Because counts are faster than time ranges on every server

explanation: The sample uses -Count rather than an end time "to avoid differences due to snapshot data": the snapshot can change while the comparison runs.
